datapoint: Gender pay gap (difference in average pay levels as a % of men's average pay level)
kpi_codes: SOC-ECART-MOY-HOR SOC-ECART-MOY-AN SOC-REMU-NB-F SOC-REMU-NB-H SOC-REMU-MOY-HOR-F SOC-REMU-MOY-HOR-H SOC-REMU-MOY-AN-F SOC-REMU-MOY-AN-H SOC-REMU-TOT-HOR-F SOC-REMU-TOT-HOR-H SOC-REMU-TOT-AN-F SOC-REMU-TOT-AN-H
note: Pay level = gross annual pay and the corresponding gross hourly pay (Art. 3.1 b): both gaps. The entity enters averages and headcounts; the tool calculates the gap at every level from the totals (Formula aggregation), so the group gap is exact.

datapoint: Gender pay gap in complementary or variable components
note: Average over the workers who receive variable pay (the directive does not say; usual practice, to check against national law). Recalculated at every level from the totals.

datapoint: Median gender pay gap
note: Hourly and annual. Entered by the entity; no group value, because a median cannot be derived from the medians of the entities.

datapoint: Median gender pay gap in complementary or variable components
note: Entered by the entity; no group value.

datapoint: Proportion of female and male workers receiving complementary or variable components
note: Calculated from the counts at every level.

datapoint: Proportion of female and male workers in each quartile pay band
kpi_codes: SOC-QUARTILE-1-F SOC-QUARTILE-1-H SOC-QUARTILE-2-F SOC-QUARTILE-2-H SOC-QUARTILE-3-F SOC-QUARTILE-3-H SOC-QUARTILE-4-F SOC-QUARTILE-4-H
note: Share of women entered per quartile, share of men calculated (100% minus women). No group value: quartiles cannot be derived from those of the entities.

datapoint: Gender pay gap by category of workers, broken down by basic wage or salary and variable components
note: Table answer: one row per category (categories are set by each employer), with the number of women and men and the two gaps.

datapoint: Employers with 250 workers or more: report every year, first by 7 June 2027
note: Thresholds and dates in the description; national law sets the exact dates.

datapoint: Employers with 150 to 249 workers: report every three years, first by 7 June 2027
Employers with 100 to 149 workers: report every three years, first by 7 June 2031
Employers with fewer than 100 workers may report voluntarily
note: Optional yes / no (the row is a « may »): it says whether the employer reports this year. An employer that does not report answers N/A to all the pay data.

datapoint: Accuracy confirmed by management after consulting workers' representatives
Information (a) to (g) sent to the monitoring authority; (a) to (f) may be published
Member State may compile (a) to (f) itself from administrative data
note: An option for the Member State: nothing for the employer to collect.

datapoint: Information (g) provided to all workers and their representatives
Answer requests for clarification; remedy gaps that are not justified
note: A process with workers and authorities: not a value per period. The joint pay assessment (Art. 10) follows it.

Content of the joint pay assessment (analysis, reasons, measures, evaluation)
note: A document written with the workers' representatives (writing a report is out of scope). Its figures by category are in SOC-ECART-CATEGORIES.

datapoint: Joint pay assessment made available to workers and sent to the monitoring body
